title: openai-v1-chat-stop-demux-stream-fallback-normalizer
author: Priya Kaur
release_notes: Normalization of /v1/chat stop signals and stream fallback to stable framing for tool-calls; no API surface break.
description:
Motivation and summary:
This PR brings parity improvements for the OpenAI /v1/chat.completions surface focused on: (1) demultiplexing 'stop' signals that mix arrays and token-level heuristics, (2) providing a deterministic fallback path when streaming encounters tool/function-call boundaries, and (3) normalizing logprob/role metadata in structured responses so downstream SDKs receive stable envelopes. The goal is to reduce customer migration friction for chat parity while improving streaming stability for tool-calling workloads.

What changed (high level):
- Added a StopDemux module that canonicalizes stop inputs (string | array | regex-like tokens) into a unified internal predicate used by the streaming agent.
- Implemented StreamFallbackCoordinator: when the streaming pipeline detects an impending tool/function call boundary or partial JSON emission, it flushes a deterministic final chunk and seamlessly switches to a framed non-stream mode for the remainder of the response, avoiding truncated tools and malformed structured output.
- Normalizer for logprobs and role annotations that converts token-level logprob arrays into a concise envelope if the client requested logprobs=true. This preserves compatibility with OpenAI clients expecting token/prob pairs while keeping streaming deltas small.
- Tests and integration harness updates to exercise mixed stop forms and tool-calls under high-concurrency, including a synthetic replay of a customer prompt that surfaced earlier truncation issues.

Commits (summary):
- 1a2b3c4: add stop demux and unit tests
- 2b3c4d5: implement stream fallback coordinator and integration tests
- 3c4d5e6: normalize logprob envelope and role metadata serializer
- 4d5e6f7: update chatv1 adapter to use new canonical stop predicate
- 5e6f7g8: add e2e harness scenarios and CI flaky test fixes

Files touched (illustrative):
- runtime/streaming/stop_demux.go (new) - core canonicalizer for stop inputs
- runtime/streaming/fallback_coordinator.go (new) - arbitration logic for streaming->framed fallback
- runtime/structured/role_logprob_normalizer.go (modified) - output envelope changes
- api/adapters/openai_chat_adapter.go (modified) - wire new components into /v1/chat handler
- tests/e2e/fixtures/stop_variants.json (new) - replay corpus

Small snippet (stop demux public API):
- CanonicalizeStop(input interface()) -> StopPredicate
- StopPredicate.Match(token string) bool

Review convo highlights:
- Marco Silva (reviewer): "Great separation between the demux and the streaming coordinator. Two asks: add property-based tests for exotic stop inputs and make the fallback window tunable via config with a reasonable default."
- Author (Priya): "Added quickcheck-style property tests that fuzz arrays/strings/null; added FallbackWindowMs config with default 50ms and documented in runtime/README.md."
- Ana López (reviewer): "Concern about metric cardinality when creating distinct fallback causes per request — recommend coalescing reasons."
- Author reply: "Coalesced fallback reasons into 'tool_boundary', 'malformed_json', 'timeout' enums; added a single tag on the request trace."
- Devon Carter (approver): "Verified e2e scenario. CI green locally and on GHA; approved for cherry-pick to release/* if we want the backport."

CI and QA notes:
- GitHub Actions: unit (pass), integration (pass), e2e (pass), lint (pass). One flaky test (stream/heartbeat_test) was stabilized by increasing the emulated scheduler quantum in the harness.
- Performance: microbench shows <3% median latency increase for non-streaming requests; streaming tool-call flows see a 10-15% decrease in truncation-related retries.

Backward compatibility and migration:
- API contract unchanged: incoming /v1/chat parameters continue to accept 'stop' as string or list. Internally we canonicalize — no client change required.
- For clients that parse token-level logprob arrays, the envelope is preserved when logprobs=true; the normalizer emits a compact token/prob list and a 'logprob_format' header set to 'compact-v1' so SDKs can detect the shape.

Merge details:
- Merge method: squash and merge
- Merged by: Ana López
- Changelog: added to v0.42.0 changelog under 'OpenAI compatibility' as 'robust stop handling and streaming fallback for tool-calls'

Follow-ups and TODOs:
- ENG-2459: Add telemetry to measure how often fallbacks occur by customer (privacy-safe sampling).
- ENG-2460: Expose a user-facing parameter to prefer framed-mode for responses that will include heavy JSON/tool payloads.
- Cleanup: remove a couple of internal debug flags after one-week canary across dedicated clusters.

Notes for on-call / SRE:
- If customers report double outputs or partial tool-call duplications, check the 'stream_fallback_reason' tag in traces and correlate with FallbackWindowMs setting.
- Rollout plan: gradual canary to 10% of hosted traffic for 48h, then 50% for 24h, full rollout. This PR was deployed to canary and monitored for 72h with no regressions.
